questions.question: What is the exact value of sin 60°?
questions.explain: In the 30-60-90 triangle, sin 60° = opposite/hypotenuse = √3/2. The most common trap is swapping the values: sin 60° is NOT 1/2 (that is sin 30° or cos 60°).

questions.question: What is the reference angle for 210°?
questions.explain: 210° lies in Quadrant III, so the reference angle is 210° − 180° = 30°. A frequent error is subtracting from 360° (giving 150°), which is the supplementary angle, not the reference angle.

questions.question: What is the exact value of cos 45°?
questions.explain: In the 45-45-90 triangle, cos 45° = adjacent/hypotenuse = 1/√2 = √2/2. Students often reach for √3/2 (which belongs to the 30-60-90 triangle) or 1/2 (which is cos 60°).

questions.question: Maya and Jake stand at opposite ends of a straight 100 m section of lake shore. Maya measures the angle to a kayak as 30° and Jake measures it as 60°, both angles taken from the shore line. How far is the kayak from Jake?
questions.explain: The angles give C = 90°. Using the Sine Law, side a (Jake-to-kayak) = c·sin A / sin C = 100·sin 30° / sin 90° = 50 m. The 86.6 m answer is side b (Maya-to-kayak), a common mix-up of which side you actually need.

questions.question: Two kayakers leave the same dock in Qualicum Beach. One paddles 5 km due east; the other paddles 7 km at 60° north of east. How far apart are they now (nearest 0.01 km)?
questions.explain: Law of Cosines: c² = 5² + 7² − 2(5)(7)cos 60° = 74 − 35 = 39, so c = √39 ≈ 6.24 km. The 8.60 km trap comes from dropping the −2ab cos θ term (treating it as a right triangle); 2.00 km comes from using cos 0° = 1 instead of cos 60° = 0.5.

questions.question: Using the unit circle, what is the exact value of sin 150°?
questions.explain: 150° is in Quadrant II where sine is positive. The reference angle is 180° − 150° = 30°, so sin 150° = sin 30° = 1/2. The most common mistake is writing −1/2 by forgetting that sine is positive in QII.

questions.question: You are given angle A = 30°, side a = 5 m, and side b = 8 m (the SSA arrangement). How many distinct triangles can be formed?
questions.explain: Check the ambiguous case: b sin A = 8 sin 30° = 4. Since 4 < a < b (i.e., 4 < 5 < 8), two triangles are possible. The biggest misconception is assuming SSA always yields a unique triangle like SAS or SSS.

questions.question: At the Seaforth Fair, a Ferris wheel has radius 10 m and its centre is 12 m above the ground. A passenger boards at the very bottom of the wheel. After the wheel has rotated 120° clockwise, how high above the ground is the passenger?
questions.explain: Starting at 270° (bottom), 120° clockwise gives 270° − 120° = 150°. Height above centre = 10 sin 150° = 10(1/2) = 5 m, so total height = 12 + 5 = 17 m. The 7 m trap subtracts the 5 m instead of adding it (sign error on sin in QII).
